exam_scheme.note: The National Science Olympiad Programme is organized by the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE - TIFR) in collaboration with the Indian Association of Physics Teachers (IAPT), Association of Chemistry Teachers (ACT), and Association of Teachers in Biological Sciences (ATBS). The programme is the official national pathway leading to India representation at the International Olympiads in Physics (IPhO), Chemistry (IChO), Biology (IBO), Astronomy (IAO), and Junior Science (IJSO). It follows a rigorous 5-stage selection hierarchy: Stage 1 is the National Standard Examination (NSEP, NSEC, NSEB, NSEA, NSEJS) conducted by IAPT consisting of 60 multiple-choice questions (216 marks, 120 minutes, +3 marks for correct, -1 for wrong). Stage 2 is the Indian National Olympiad (INPhO, INChO, INBO, INAO, INJSO) conducted by HBCSE for the top ~300 students per subject, featuring in-depth theoretical and analytical problems. Stage 3 is the Orientation-cum-Selection Camp (OCSC) at HBCSE (~35 students per subject; intensive theoretical and experimental laboratory tests). Stage 4 is Pre-Departure Training (PDT) for the selected 4-5 member Indian national team, culminating in Stage 5: participation in the International Olympiads.
